threads.body: [Style] This javaagent helper is only referenced from the same package, so making it public exposes more API than needed, and repository Java style explicitly says not to add `final` to classes under `javaagent/src/main`. Please keep it package-private and non-final.

replies.body:
Addressed in 20e3d21d8d6c0d4248059434fbcc400e7ade002e.

Analysis: ServletConfig is only consumed within its javaagent package, so package-private visibility is sufficient, and javaagent implementation classes intentionally remain non-final.

Upsides: Keeps the helper out of the exposed implementation surface and follows the javaagent class-style rule.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: The PR promises that the deprecated setter remains an include-only alias, but all existing callers were migrated and no test invokes this forwarding path. Please retain coverage that calls `setCaptureRequestParameters(...)` and verifies the selected parameter is captured so this compatibility contract cannot regress.

replies.body:
Addressed in fb962f707a6ecb117e1b78a804804b6d52a88727.

Analysis: The existing servlet 3.0 and 5.0 library fixtures already verify that `test-parameter` is captured. Configuring those fixtures through the deprecated setter directly exercises its include-only forwarding contract, with member-scoped suppressions documenting the intentional compatibility coverage.

Upsides: Prevents regressions in both deprecated aliases while reusing the existing end-to-end request-parameter assertions.

Downsides: The fixtures intentionally depend on deprecated APIs until those APIs are removed in 3.0.

    builder,
